statement: The function returns a result r, and r equals the number of distinct primes p such that p divides nums[i] for at least one index i with 0 ≤ i < len(nums). Here a prime is an integer p > 1 whose only positive divisors are 1 and p, and 'p divides nums[i]' means there exists an integer k with nums[i] = p·k. In set notation, r = |{ p : p is prime and ∃ i, 0 ≤ i < len(nums) and p divides nums[i] }|.
preconditions: 1 ≤ len(nums) ≤ 10^4, and for every i with 0 ≤ i < len(nums), 2 ≤ nums[i] ≤ 1000 (nums[i] read as a mathematical integer).

statement: The function returns a result r for every input satisfying the preconditions; it does not fail (no panic, no out-of-bounds access, and no arithmetic overflow).
preconditions: 1 ≤ len(nums) ≤ 10^4, and for every i with 0 ≤ i < len(nums), 2 ≤ nums[i] ≤ 1000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, 1 ≤ r.
preconditions: 1 ≤ len(nums) ≤ 10^4, and for every i with 0 ≤ i < len(nums), 2 ≤ nums[i] ≤ 1000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r ≤ 168.
preconditions: 1 ≤ len(nums) ≤ 10^4, and for every i with 0 ≤ i < len(nums), 2 ≤ nums[i] ≤ 1000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r ≤ 4 * len(nums).
preconditions: 1 ≤ len(nums) ≤ 10^4, and for every i with 0 ≤ i < len(nums), 2 ≤ nums[i] ≤ 1000.

statement: Whenever the function returns r1 on nums1 and r2 on nums2, r1 = r2.
preconditions: Both nums1 and nums2 satisfy 1 ≤ len ≤ 10^4 and all entries lie in [2,1000]. Also nums2 is a permutation (reordering) of nums1: there is a bijection φ from the indices of nums1 to the indices of nums2 with nums2[φ(i)] = nums1[i] for every i.

statement: Whenever the function returns r1 on nums1 and r2 on nums2, r2 ≤ r1.
preconditions: Both nums1 and nums2 satisfy 1 ≤ len ≤ 10^4 and all entries lie in [2,1000]. For every prime p, if p divides nums2[i] for some i, then p divides nums1[j] for some j. Equivalently, the set of primes dividing at least one element of nums2 is contained in the corresponding set for nums1.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r = 1 if and only if there exists a prime p such that every element nums[i] is a power of p, i.e., for each i with 0 ≤ i < len(nums) there is an integer k_i ≥ 1 with nums[i] = p^{k_i}.
preconditions: 1 ≤ len(nums) ≤ 10^4, and for every i with 0 ≤ i < len(nums), 2 ≤ nums[i] ≤ 1000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r ≤ π(M), where π(M) is the number of primes p with p ≤ M.
preconditions: 1 ≤ len(nums) ≤ 10^4, and for every i with 0 ≤ i < len(nums), 2 ≤ nums[i] ≤ 1000. Let M = max { nums[i] : 0 ≤ i < len(nums) }, which is well-defined because len(nums) ≥ 1.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every index i with 0 ≤ i < len(nums), r ≥ d(nums[i]).
preconditions: 1 ≤ len(nums) ≤ 10^4, and for every i with 0 ≤ i < len(nums), 2 ≤ nums[i] ≤ 1000. For an integer x ≥ 2, let d(x) be the number of distinct primes dividing x.

statement: Whenever the function returns r on nums and r' on nums', r = r'.
preconditions: nums satisfies 1 ≤ len(nums) ≤ 10^4 and all entries lie in [2,1000], and len(nums) ≥ 2. Let j and k be indices with 0 ≤ j < len(nums), 0 ≤ k < len(nums), j ≠ k, and nums[j] divides nums[k]. Let nums' be the slice obtained from nums by deleting the element at index j; it has length len(nums)-1 and still satisfies the basic constraints.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, there exist r distinct primes p_1 < p_2 < ... < p_r such that: (i) for every t with 1 ≤ t ≤ r, p_t divides nums[i] for some i with 0 ≤ i < len(nums); and (ii) for every prime q, if q divides nums[i] for some i, then q = p_t for some t with 1 ≤ t ≤ r.
preconditions: 1 ≤ len(nums) ≤ 10^4, and for every i with 0 ≤ i < len(nums), 2 ≤ nums[i] ≤ 1000.

statement: Whenever the function returns r on nums and r' on nums ++ [x], r' = r + |{ p : p is prime, p divides x, and for every i with 0 ≤ i < len(nums), p does not divide nums[i] }|.
preconditions: nums satisfies 1 ≤ len(nums) ≤ 10^4 and every nums[i] lies in [2,1000]; x is an integer with 2 ≤ x ≤ 1000; and len(nums) < 10^4 so that nums ++ [x] also satisfies the length constraint.

statement: Whenever the function returns r on nums and r' on nums', r' = r - |{ p : p is prime, p divides nums[j], and for every i with 0 ≤ i < len(nums) and i ≠ j, p does not divide nums[i] }|.
preconditions: nums satisfies 1 ≤ len(nums) ≤ 10^4 and every entry lies in [2,1000]; len(nums) ≥ 2; j is an index with 0 ≤ j < len(nums); and nums' is the slice obtained from nums by deleting nums[j].
